[TIME_CHECK:evening]
[TIME_ADVANCE:5m]
[WARES:none]

[SAY:Korrag]"What is this place called?" you mutter aloud to the wind. "Which way to the nearest town?"

Only the rattle of dry scrub answers. The copper-scented ink on your map labels this desolate crossing as Ashenveil. Due north lies the checkpoint at Redford Crossing, barred by soldiers and dogs. Beyond that iron blockade sits Oakhaven, the walled borough where your promised pouch of silver waits. To the south lies only the dead frontier you just crossed. The east track winds deep into the rotting scrub, bypassing the river gate entirely.

[SUGGEST:Take the eastern bypass track|Scout the northern checkpoint|Inspect the bone-casket cargo]

turns.raw:
[TIME_CHECK:evening]
[TIME_ADVANCE:10m]
[SOUNDSCAPE:The Crossroads of Ashenveil|enclosure=open;setting=wilderness;biome=temperate;quiet=normal;allows=wind,animals,bells;forbid=none]

You squint down at the map. The parchment is stiff with dried salt and witch-blood. The dark ink sits right where your boots stand. Ashenveil is no lost valley. It is the dead scrub wrapping around Hushwick itself. 

The village lies barely a mile north-east toward the coast. Close enough to smell the salt over the rot. But the rutted road cuts through the checkpoint first. The soldiers hold the river bridge. Their iron bell clangs again, dull and heavy. 

Dogs whine in the distance. The cart axle groans under the bone-casket.

[SUGGEST:Haul cart down the north road|Scout east toward the coastline|Check the casket before moving]

turns.action: I leave the cart hidden in the scrub and walk north-east, skirting the checkpoint, into Hushwick itself.

[TIME_CHECK:evening]
[TIME_ADVANCE:25m]
[LOCATION:Hushwick]
[LOCATION_DESC:A sprawling, wall-less coastal village of huddled timber and thatch cottages. Salt spray mingles with chimney smoke. The sea churns grey to the northeast.]
[LOCATION_SIZE:medium|15]
[EXIT:The Green|Open commons at the heart of the village]
[EXIT:The Grey Lion|Weather-beaten wooden inn near the village edge]
[EXIT:Neirgear's Cellar|Sunken stone tavern smelling of bitter ale]
[EXIT:The Harbour|Rocky quayside and slipways on the eastern shore]
[LOCATION_RESIDENT:Drasdur]
[LOCATION_RESIDENT:Wrathaes]

You haul the wagon into the thickest thorns. The bone-casket stays lashed tight under the grease-cloth. 

The scrub tears at your wool cloak. You circle wide around the river bridge. No dogs catch the scent. Soon your boots hit salt-grass. 

Hushwick reeks of dried cod, peat fires, and brine. Cobbled paths wind between dark timber houses. Folk give your mail coat a wide berth. Across the square sits a weathered tavern, its door creaking in the gale.

[SUGGEST:Enter The Grey Lion|Head to The Green|Walk to the harbour]

opening:
[TIME_CHECK:evening]
[TIME_ADVANCE:10m]
[LOCATION_DESC:A desolate four-way junction choked in grey grit, surrounded by twisted, leafless scrub. To the north lies the militarized river road toward Redford Crossing, while the southern track leads back toward the border barrens. East and west stretch choked paths into the rotting brush.]
[LOCATION_SIZE:medium|20]
[EXIT:North road|Rutted trail leading toward Redford Crossing]
[EXIT:East track|Overgrown path into the grey scrub]
[EXIT:West trail|Stony incline toward the ridge]
[QUEST:The Redford Crossing|active]
[QUEST_STEP:The Redford Crossing|Navigate past the river checkpoint to reach Oakhaven|false]

The wind tastes of bitter chimney ash and sour damp. A heavy wooden cart sits mired in the grit, bearing a long bone-casket lashed tight under oilcloth. Your traveler's map shows a bypass off the main road, inked in dark, sticky pigment that smells faintly of copper. From the north road, the hollow clang of an iron checkpoint bell drifts through the gloom, accompanied by the muffled bark of guard hounds. 

[SUGGEST:Examine the map's route|Check the casket's lashings|Scout the northern road]
